result.summary: Updates the test framework's P2PConnection v1 message parser to verify network magic bytes only after receiving a full 24-byte header, matching bitcoind's V1Transport behavior. Previously, the test framework rejected the stream after receiving only 4 bytes if they did not match the magic.
result.problem: If network socket data arrives in small chunks, P2PConnection could disconnect after reading 4 bytes. Because bitcoind's V2Transport::ShouldReconnectV1 only attempts a v1 reconnect if at least a full 24-byte header was sent before peer disconnection, premature disconnection causes the node not to reconnect, leading p2p_v2_encrypted.py to time out.
evidence: Author notes the failure is reproducible under forced chunked socket sends: "This was found -- and can be reproduced -- by using a reproducer patch, that forces all socket sends to use smaller chunking. For the run with the reproducer see #36724."
Related to issue #36726 regarding test errors from socket data chunking assumptions.
result.scope_notes: A minimal 1-commit (+2/-3) fix in the Python test framework.
result.card: Updates P2PConnection in the Python test framework to wait for the complete 24-byte v1 header before validating magic bytes, mirroring bitcoind's V1Transport::readHeader. Currently, if socket reads are chunked in pieces under 24 bytes, P2PConnection disconnects too early, preventing bitcoind from triggering its v2-to-v1 downgrade fallback and causing p2p_v2_encrypted.py to hang or time out. Author demonstrated the failure using a forced-chunking reproducer in PR #36724.

risk.why: Only touches Python test framework socket parsing, with no effect on node runtime or release code.
